title: Echoes of Star Stories: Integrating Indigenous narratives into modern stellar astrophysics
comment: 7 pages, accepted for publication in Proceedings of Oxford XIII / IAU Symposium 399
summary: Indigenous narratives have long preserved observations of celestial phenomena, offering insights that resonate with modern astrophysical research. Deeply embedded in cultural traditions, these stories describe events such as stellar variability, supernovae, eclipses, and planetary alignments. Indigenous communities have also used the stars for navigation and calendar systems, reflecting a sophisticated understanding of celestial patterns. These narratives not only complement historical records but offer human-centric perspectives on stellar life cycles that often parallel modern models. Drawing from traditions from diverse Indigenous communities - including Aboriginal Australians, Pueblo peoples, Inuit, and Polynesians - this paper highlights the profound connections between Indigenous knowledge and stellar astrophysics. Integrating these traditions acknowledges their value, safeguards their relevance in the Space Age, and fosters mutual learning through cross-cultural collaboration. We explore how such narratives can enrich education, public engagement, and even inspire scientific hypotheses, bridging cultural heritage and modern astrophysics.

AI.tldr: This paper explores how Indigenous narratives from Aboriginal Australian, Pueblo, Inuit, and Polynesian cultures describe celestial phenomena (stellar variability, supernovae, eclipses, planetary alignments, navigation, and calendar systems) and demonstrates their alignment with modern stellar astrophysics, advocating for integration of these knowledge systems in education, public engagement, and scientific inquiry.
AI.motivation: To highlight the profound connections between Indigenous knowledge and stellar astrophysics, acknowledging the value of Indigenous narratives as complementary to modern astrophysical models, and to foster cross-cultural collaboration that safeguards Indigenous knowledge in the Space Age.
AI.method: Drawing from diverse Indigenous traditions (Aboriginal Australians, Pueblo peoples, Inuit, Polynesians) and comparing their celestial narratives with modern astrophysical understanding of stellar variability, supernovae, eclipses, planetary alignments, navigation, and calendar systems.
AI.result: Indigenous narratives describe stellar phenomena (variability, supernovae, eclipses, planetary alignments) and demonstrate sophisticated astronomical knowledge (navigation, calendars) that often parallels modern astrophysical models.
AI.conclusion: Integrating Indigenous knowledge with modern astrophysics enriches education and public engagement, safeguards cultural heritage, and can inspire scientific hypotheses through mutual learning and cross-cultural collaboration.

title: Rate of caustic crossing microlensing events in stellar binary lenses with significant orbital motion
comment: 17 pages, 12 figures; Accepted for publication in ApJ
summary: Binary lens microlensing events in which the source crosses a caustic produce sharp, distinctive magnification peaks and can therefore be readily identified. In this paper, we explore the importance of binary orbital motion for the binary lens caustic crossing cross section. If the orbital timescale of the binary system is smaller than the Einstein ring crossing timescale, the caustics sweep out a larger area in the source plane, generally enhancing the cross section. We find that face-on binaries in circular orbits exhibit a substantial increase (up to 4$\times$) in the cross section for caustic crossings. However, highly inclined orbits produce a net decrease relative to a static face-on binary with the same semi-major axis. Using a sample of ~$2800$ synthetic binary microlensing events drawn from a realistic Milky Way population-synthesis model, we calculate the average change in the caustic crossing cross section for individual systems with and without orbital motion. Although orbital motion can significantly alter the cross section for specific geometries, we find that, when averaged over the full population, it produces only a small, negligible increase of ~$0.1\%$ in the average cross section. We also compute the overall rate of caustic crossing binary events in the simulated sample and find that, with sufficiently dense photometric sampling, $6.3 \pm 0.2\%$ of microlensing events with impact parameter $u_0 < 1$ should exhibit caustic crossings. This rate depends on the distributions of binary separation, mass ratio, and multiplicity of stars and compact objects, and can therefore be used to test our understanding of these underlying properties.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates how binary orbital motion affects caustic crossing cross sections in binary lens microlensing events. While orbital motion can significantly alter cross sections for specific geometries (enhancing for face-on circular orbits, decreasing for highly inclined orbits), when averaged over a realistic Milky Way population (~2800 synthetic events), the net effect is negligible (~0.1% increase). The overall caustic crossing rate is estimated at 6.3±0.2% for events with impact parameter u0<1, which can be used to test binary properties like separation, mass ratio, and multiplicity.
AI.motivation: To understand the importance of binary orbital motion on the binary lens caustic crossing cross section, which affects the detectability and interpretation of binary microlensing events.
AI.method: Analytical calculations of caustic crossing cross sections with orbital motion for different binary geometries, combined with a population-synthesis model of ~2800 synthetic binary microlensing events drawn from a realistic Milky Way model.
AI.result: Face-on circular binaries show up to 4× increase in cross section; highly inclined orbits show a net decrease. Population-averaged effect is a negligible ~0.1% increase. The overall caustic crossing rate is 6.3±0.2% for u0<1 events.
AI.conclusion: Orbital motion does not significantly alter the average caustic crossing cross section for binary lens events, but the measured caustic crossing rate can serve as a probe of binary separation, mass ratio, and multiplicity distributions in the Milky Way.

title: Magnetically guided accretion and extremely slow rotation in a metal-enriched white dwarf
summary: White dwarfs that show atmospheric metal enrichment offer a direct window into the bulk composition of exoplanetary material and provide some of the most direct constraints on the building blocks of rocky exoplanetary systems. Recent work has suggested that magnetic fields may influence how this material is accreted, potentially channelling debris along field lines and retaining it near magnetic poles rather than allowing it to be redistributed uniformly across the stellar surface. Here we report the discovery of photometric, spectroscopic, and spectropolarimetric variability in the magnetic DZ white dwarf WD1532+129, revealing a rotation period of about 289 days, by far the longest yet directly measured for any degenerate star. The observed period may result from the combined effect of angular-momentum loss during the evolution leading to the white dwarf stage and an unusually slowly rotating progenitor, perhaps a magnetic Ap star. The white dwarf exhibits surface abundance inhomogeneities, with metals concentrated near both magnetic poles, and the observed modulation is consistent with localised metal-rich regions aligned with the magnetic geometry. WD1532+129 is the third of the four known magnetic DZ white dwarfs within 20 pc to show evidence for polar metal enhancement, indicating that magnetically guided inhomogeneities are a common property of magnetic metal-enriched white dwarfs.

AI.tldr: Discovery of WD1532+129, a magnetic DZ white dwarf with a ~289-day rotation period—the longest ever directly measured for a degenerate star—showing metals concentrated near magnetic poles, suggesting magnetically guided accretion is common among magnetic metal-enriched white dwarfs.
AI.motivation: To understand how magnetic fields influence the accretion and distribution of exoplanetary material onto white dwarfs, as metal-enriched white dwarfs provide direct constraints on the composition of rocky exoplanetary material.
AI.method: Photometric, spectroscopic, and spectropolarimetric observations of WD1532+129, measuring its rotation period and correlating surface abundance variations with magnetic geometry.
AI.result: WD1532+129 has a rotation period of ~289 days, the longest directly measured for any degenerate star. Metals are inhomogeneously distributed and concentrated near both magnetic poles.
AI.conclusion: Magnetically guided metal inhomogeneities are a common property of magnetic DZ white dwarfs, with WD1532+129 being the third of four known such objects within 20 pc showing polar metal enhancement.

title: Spectral evolution of mildly relativistic electrons in solar flares
summary: Solar flares are a powerful engine capable of accelerating ambient plasma particles to high nonthermal energies. A key characteristic of these particles is their energy spectrum. Numerous studies of nonthermal hard X-ray emission established that a typical spectral evolution of the nonthermal electrons with energies of dozens keV follows a soft-hard-soft pattern in impulsive events and soft-hard-harder pattern in some long-duration events. Here we extend the study of the spectral evolution to the case of flare-accelerated mildly relativistic electrons primarily responsible for the flare microwave emission. We examine the spatially resolved microwave emission observed with the Expanded Owens Valley Solar Array in twelve solar flares and find that they also typically follow a soft-hard-soft spectral evolution. However, the revealed spectral evolution of the mildly relativistic electrons covers the spectral index range from 2-4 to 15 or more and, thus, is much more prominent than for the X-ray-producing electrons. The evolution of the spectral index is closely correlated with the emission flux and does not show any noticeable time delay. The spectral index displays a prominent correlation with the brightness temperature with a pattern similar to all events considered. We conclude that the revealed relationships and the evolutionary pattern is an inherent property of particle acceleration in the solar flares.

AI.tldr: This study analyzes microwave emission from 12 solar flares using EOVSA data and finds that mildly relativistic electrons follow a soft-hard-soft spectral evolution, with a much wider spectral index range (2-4 to 15+) than X-ray-producing electrons, and show strong correlation with emission flux and brightness temperature.
AI.motivation: To extend the study of spectral evolution from nonthermal X-ray electrons (tens of keV) to mildly relativistic electrons responsible for flare microwave emission, and to understand their spectral behavior patterns.
AI.method: Spatially resolved microwave observations from the Expanded Owens Valley Solar Array (EOVSA) were examined in twelve solar flares, analyzing the spectral evolution of mildly relativistic electrons.
AI.result: Mildly relativistic electrons follow a soft-hard-soft spectral evolution pattern with a spectral index range of 2-4 to 15+, much wider than X-ray electrons. Spectral evolution correlates closely with emission flux with no noticeable time delay, and shows prominent correlation with brightness temperature.
AI.conclusion: The revealed relationships and evolutionary pattern are inherent properties of particle acceleration in solar flares.

title: Population synthesis of delta Scuti stars: the instability strip, period-luminosity relation, and large-separation distribution
summary: Interpreting the observed properties of intermediate-mass stars requires accounting for rotation, binarity, intrinsic population diversity, and measurement uncertainty. We combine these effects in population-synthesis models of 1.4-2.5 M$_{\odot}$ stars that include pulsation properties of $δ$ Sct variables. The synthetic populations successfully reproduce the distributions of stars observed in young associations, validating the mapping between intrinsic and observed stellar properties. Using these models, we infer a semi-empirical $δ$ Sct instability strip by matching synthetic and observed populations. The resulting instability strip is systematically hotter than widely used theoretical prescriptions, implying that $δ$ Sct stars are on average 0.1 M$_{\odot}$ more massive than previously assumed, with 95% of the population spanning approximately 1.50-2.30 M$_{\odot}$. We then investigate the $δ$ Sct period-luminosity relation and reproduce its recently identified second ridge with mixture models in which roughly one-third of stars have the fifth or sixth radial overtone as their dominant mode; the fraction increases in younger populations. In contrast, unresolved binarity does not account for the second ridge. Finally, we predict the population-wide distribution of asteroseismic large separations, $Δν$, finding a peak between 6 and 7 d$^{-1}$, in agreement with recent observations. We also demonstrate that $Δν$ is most reliably measured with the échelle technique, while autocorrelation methods can produce spurious detections when used in isolation. These results show that population synthesis provides a powerful framework for interpreting populations of $δ$ Sct stars and for linking stellar evolution, pulsation, and observation.

AI.tldr: Population-synthesis models of 1.4-2.5 M☉ stars incorporating rotation, binarity, and pulsation properties successfully reproduce observed δ Sct star distributions. The models yield a semi-empirical instability strip systematically hotter than theoretical prescriptions, implying δ Sct stars are ~0.1 M☉ more massive than previously thought. The second ridge in the period-luminosity relation is explained by ~1/3 of stars pulsating in fifth/sixth radial overtones (not binarity), and the predicted Δν distribution peaks at 6-7 d⁻¹, matching observations.
AI.motivation: To interpret observed properties of intermediate-mass δ Sct stars by accounting for rotation, binarity, population diversity, and measurement uncertainty, and to validate population-synthesis models as a framework linking stellar evolution, pulsation, and observations.
AI.method: Population-synthesis models of 1.4-2.5 M☉ stars including rotation, binarity, and δ Sct pulsation properties; comparison with observed distributions in young associations; mixture models for period-luminosity relation analysis; échelle and autocorrelation techniques for Δν measurement.
AI.result: Synthetic populations reproduce observed distributions; derived instability strip is systematically hotter, implying 0.1 M☉ higher masses (95% of population in 1.50-2.30 M☉ range); second ridge in period-luminosity relation explained by ~1/3 of stars in 5th/6th radial overtones; Δν peaks at 6-7 d⁻¹; échelle technique is more reliable than autocorrelation for Δν measurement.
AI.conclusion: Population synthesis is a powerful framework for interpreting δ Sct star populations and linking stellar evolution, pulsation, and observation.

title: Ensemble Kinematic Ages for 1.5 Million LAMOST Stars
summary: We present a framework for inferring stellar ages from spectroscopic stellar parameters, calibrated with ensemble kinematics by averaging over the median vertical action, $J_z$, for stars with similar atmospheric and chemical properties, yielding self-consistent age estimates across the Hertzsprung-Russell (HR) diagram. We refer to these ages as ensemble kinematic ages as the age scale is calibrated from the average kinematics of ensembles of stars with similar stellar parameters. Individual stellar kinematics are not used in assigning ages. We validate the method against subgiant ages, achieving an accuracy of ~30%, comparable to [C/N]-based estimates. We find a clear age-$J_z$ relations that enable age inference up to ~10 Gyr for both the high- and low-$α$ disks. Applying this framework to 1.5 million LAMOST stars, we derive ages for subgiants and giants with typical uncertainties of ~2 Gyr. The inferred ages agree well with literature age catalogs, with no significant systematic trends as a function of $\log g$. We also demonstrate the potential of empirical isochrones to calibrate theoretical stellar models. We identify an old (~7 Gyr) population within the low-$α$ disk but draw no firm conclusions. Although ensemble kinematic ages are statistical and sensitive to selection effects, Galactic potential assumptions, and Galactic location, they provide a robust population-level tool for Galactic archaeology, complementing traditional age indicators and extending age estimates across the full HR diagram.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a method for inferring stellar ages from spectroscopic parameters by calibrating with ensemble kinematics via median vertical action $J_z$, achieving ~30% accuracy (~2 Gyr uncertainties) for subgiants and giants, validated across 1.5 million LAMOST stars.
AI.motivation: Existing stellar age estimation methods are limited in scope across the HR diagram; the authors aim to provide a self-consistent, population-level age inference framework that complements traditional indicators and extends age estimates to a broader range of stellar types.
AI.method: Ensemble kinematic ages are derived by averaging median vertical action $J_z$ over stars with similar atmospheric and chemical parameters, calibrating an age scale from ensemble kinematics without using individual stellar kinematics. The method is validated against subgiant ages and applied to 1.5 million LAMOST stars.
AI.result: Accuracy ~30% comparable to [C/N]-based estimates; clear age-$J_z$ relations found for high- and low-$\alpha$ disks up to ~10 Gyr; typical uncertainties ~2 Gyr for subgiants and giants; ages agree with literature without significant $\log g$ systematics; an old (~7 Gyr) population identified in the low-$\alpha$ disk.
AI.conclusion: Ensemble kinematic ages are statistical and sensitive to selection effects, Galactic potential, and location, but provide a robust population-level tool for Galactic archaeology, complementing traditional age indicators across the full HR diagram.

title: Discovery of a radio-flaring M dwarf in a commensal transient search of the LADUMA field
summary: We report the discovery and characterisation of MKT J032848.4-271904.6, a new radio transient identified in the LADUMA field using SARAO Science Data Processor (SDP) UHF-band images from approximately one year of MeerKAT observations. Using the Transient Pipeline (TraP) and advanced filtering techniques, we identified a number of candidate variable radio sources in the field. All but one show variability consistent with refractive interstellar scintillation, leaving MKT J032848.4-271904.6 as the sole source exhibiting intrinsic variability. In addition, MKT J032848.4-271904.6 shows intrinsic variability at 0.816 GHz, with 13 radio detections across 41 epochs and a peak flux density of 1.041+/-0.043 mJy. We associate this emission with a low-mass M-dwarf star LP 888-63, located 23 pc from the Sun and identified as a companion to the white dwarf binary system LAWD 14 / WD 0326-273. LP 888-63 displays active flaring behaviour across the electromagnetic spectrum, including multi-band optical data from MeerLICHT. TESS photometry reveals a periodic modulation in the blended light curve of 5.780+/-0.507 days, consistent with rotational variability of a mid-M dwarf. Archival ESO spectra reveal Halpha emission, confirming magnetic activity. These findings highlight the capability of MeerKAT's SDP imaging and facilities like MeerLICHT for real-time detection and characterisation of stellar transients.

AI.tldr: This paper reports the discovery of MKT J032848.4-271904.6, a new radio transient identified in MeerKAT observations. It is associated with the M-dwarf star LP 888-63 (part of the LAWD 14 binary system), showing intrinsic radio variability, optical flaring, and rotational modulation, demonstrating MeerKAT's capability for stellar transient detection.
AI.motivation: To identify and characterize new radio transients in the LADUMA field using MeerKAT observations, and to distinguish intrinsic variability from interstellar scintillation effects.
AI.method: Used the Transient Pipeline (TraP) and advanced filtering on SARAO SDP UHF-band images from ~1 year of MeerKAT data. Multi-wavelength follow-up included MeerLICHT optical data, TESS photometry, and archival ESO spectra.
AI.result: MKT J032848.4-271904.6 is the only source with intrinsic variability (0.816 GHz), detected 13 times over 41 epochs (peak flux 1.041±0.043 mJy). Associated with M-dwarf LP 888-63 (23 pc away), showing flaring across the EM spectrum, Halpha emission, and a 5.78-day rotational modulation in TESS data.
AI.conclusion: MeerKAT's SDP imaging combined with facilities like MeerLICHT enables effective real-time detection and characterization of stellar transients, as demonstrated by the identification of an active M-dwarf companion in a white dwarf binary system.

title: Detection of pulsations and a non-stable wind in IRAS 01005+7910, an object with the B[e]-phenomenon
comment: 10 pages, 3 figures, 1 table, accepted for publication in Astronomy
summary: Comparison of the spectra obtained at different observing dates shows significant variations in the complex H$α$ and H$β$ line profiles, such as a systematic increase in their emission peak strengths in 2025$÷$2026 compared to those observed in 2013 as well as a strong variability in their wind component. A detected variable radial velocity $V_{\odot}$ from $-20$ to $-68$ km/s with a standard deviation of the mean value of K$\sim$8.0 km/s can be interpreted as a result of pulsations or the presence of a companion. The stationary positions of forbidden lines with a mean radial velocity of $V_{\odot}=-51.38\pm0.26$ km/s are taken as an improved systemic velocity. Overall, a set of properties of IRAS 01005+7910 points to its status as a post-AGB star, which has undergone the hot-bottom burning phase.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes spectral variations of IRAS 01005+7910 across multiple observing epochs, finding systematic increases in Hα and Hβ emission strengths between 2013 and 2025/2026, variable radial velocities (−20 to −68 km/s, K~8.0 km/s), and a systemic velocity of −51.38±0.26 km/s from forbidden lines. The object is classified as a post-AGB star that underwent hot-bottom burning.
AI.motivation: To characterize the spectral variability and nature of IRAS 01005+7910, a candidate post-AGB star, through multi-epoch spectroscopic monitoring and radial velocity analysis.
AI.method: Multi-epoch spectroscopic observations comparing Hα and Hβ line profiles across different dates (2013 vs. 2025/2026), radial velocity measurements from different line species, and analysis of forbidden line positions to determine systemic velocity.
AI.result: Significant variability in Hα and Hβ profiles including increased emission peak strengths in later epochs and strong wind component variations. Radial velocity (V⊙) ranges from −20 to −68 km/s with K~8.0 km/s. Forbidden lines yield a systemic velocity of V⊙=−51.38±0.26 km/s.
AI.conclusion: IRAS 01005+7910 is a post-AGB star that experienced hot-bottom burning, with detected radial velocity variations likely due to pulsations or binarity.

title: Spin-spin coupling in stellar binaries
summary: Spin-orbit misalignment is increasingly observed in binary stars, but its origin remains uncertain. We study the secular spin dynamics of stellar binaries and derive the associated Cassini states. We isolate a spin-spin resonance that arises when the two stellar spin-precession frequencies become commensurate. This resonance can excite the obliquity of the secondary to high values even when the primary is only weakly tilted. Magnetic braking favors the formation of high-obliquity states, whereas tidal dissipation may suppress them. Spin-spin coupling may thus help explain the observed diversity of obliquities in young stellar binaries.

AI.tldr: This paper studies the secular spin dynamics of stellar binaries and identifies a spin-spin resonance that can excite high obliquity in the secondary star even when the primary is only weakly tilted. Magnetic braking promotes high obliquity, while tidal dissipation suppresses it, offering an explanation for the observed diversity of spin-orbit misalignments in young stellar binaries.
AI.motivation: Spin-orbit misalignment is increasingly observed in binary stars, but its origin remains uncertain. The paper aims to understand the physical mechanisms driving obliquity excitation in stellar binaries.
AI.method: The authors study secular spin dynamics of stellar binaries and derive associated Cassini states. They isolate a spin-spin resonance that occurs when the two stellar spin-precession frequencies become commensurate.
AI.result: The spin-spin resonance can excite the obliquity of the secondary star to high values even when the primary is only weakly tilted. Magnetic braking favors the formation of high-obliquity states, whereas tidal dissipation may suppress them.
AI.conclusion: Spin-spin coupling may help explain the observed diversity of obliquities in young stellar binaries.

title: Payne4GAIN: NLTE Corrections for Red Giants in Milky Way Mapper using H-Band Neural Network Emulators
comment: 20 pages, 11 figures, 4 tables. To be submitted to Open Journal of Astrophysics
summary: The majority of spectroscopic surveys assume local thermodynamic equilibrium (LTE) during the modeling of stellar spectra. This assumption begins to break down for luminous stars, like the red giants targeted by SDSS-V's Milky Way Mapper Survey in its Galactic Genesis program. In this work, we present non-LTE (NLTE) abundances for 360,000 red giant stars in Milky Way Mapper DR19, from infrared APOGEE spectra. We generate NLTE spectra using precomputed departure coefficient grids for Na, Mg, Si, Al, Ca, Ti, Mn, and Ni. To fit APOGEE spectra at scale, we train neural network emulators (NNEs) to synthesize LTE and NLTE H-band spectra. After verifying that the NNEs are accurate, we fit the APOGEE spectra with ASPCAP results that fall within the same parameter range as the training data. We find strong NLTE effects on the order of 0.1\,dex for Al, Mn, and Ti, and smaller effects for Si and Ni. We provide a catalog of the results of our LTE and NLTE fits, as well as NLTE-corrected ASPCAP abundances using a polynomial fit correction.

AI.tldr: This paper presents non-LTE (NLTE) abundances for 360,000 red giant stars from SDSS-V's Milky Way Mapper using APOGEE spectra. Neural network emulators were trained to synthesize LTE and NLTE H-band spectra, and strong NLTE effects (~0.1 dex) were found for Al, Mn, and Ti, with smaller effects for Si and Ni. A catalog of LTE and NLTE fits, plus NLTE-corrected ASPCAP abundances, is provided.
AI.motivation: The LTE assumption breaks down for luminous stars like red giants; thus, NLTE corrections are needed to obtain accurate stellar abundances for large spectroscopic surveys.
AI.method: Precomputed departure coefficient grids for Na, Mg, Si, Al, Ca, Ti, Mn, and Ni were used to generate NLTE spectra. Neural network emulators (NNEs) were trained to synthesize LTE and NLTE H-band spectra, then applied to fit APOGEE spectra with ASPCAP within the training parameter range.
AI.result: Strong NLTE effects (~0.1 dex) for Al, Mn, Ti; smaller effects for Si and Ni. A catalog of LTE and NLTE fits and NLTE-corrected ASPCAP abundances (via polynomial correction) was produced for 360,000 red giants.
AI.conclusion: NLTE corrections are significant for several elements in red giants; the neural network emulator approach enables large-scale NLTE abundance analysis, and the resulting catalogs improve the accuracy of stellar abundance measurements in the Milky Way Mapper Survey.
